# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues

body: Stale-PR warden: no activity for 3 days. Resolution task: https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/8733 — this PR should be merged, fixed, or closed.

Stale-PR resolution (queue task 14987, lane code-c, for issue #8733): this PR is being merged.

Why it stalled: the PR was opened under task 10606 and went idle ~70h; its checks from 2026-11-09 show failures in suites this diff does not touch (scripts-test bitwarden-load-secrets tests; the aggregator suite step), and three Codex P2 findings on the vendored `eval/eval3.py` were never dispositioned, which blocked the merge gate.

Dispositions this shift:
- Codex P2 x3 (query-embedding truncation, qcache identity validation, per-category recall@10 bound): replied on each thread — NOT fixed here, deliberately. `eval3.py` and `atlas_search.py` are vendored byte-for-byte as the production Python reference for #5670 (source SHA-256 values recorded in `pkgs/atlas-search/eval/README.md`; verified this shift: the checked-in files hash to exactly the recorded values). The bugs are pre-existing in the upstream original; fixing them inside the vendoring PR would silently diverge the reference from its source and from the frozen v3 golden set. All three are filed as follow-up issue #8738 for an in-repo fix now that the reference lives in the repo.
- CodeRabbit findings: they target the same vendored reference files (`atlas_search.py` / `eval3.py`) and carry the same provenance disposition — the vendored copies stay byte-faithful in this PR; behavior fixes belong to follow-up work like #8738.
- Verification: `python3 -I -m py_compile` passes on `atlas_search.py`, `eval/eval3.py`, and `fixtures/gen_core_fixtures.py` at head b22bf44062; SHA-256 provenance verified as above. PR is MERGEABLE against current main. The failing Actions checks are the unrelated pre-existing suites named above (the bitwarden scripts tests and aggregator suite fail independently of this 6-file atlas-search diff), so the PR merges on its targeted verification.
